plugin.name: Hanshuang Pojia
plugin.description: Statically triage APK, AAB, IPA, DEX, ELF, PE, Mach-O and archive samples: format, manifest facts, permissions, exported components, native hardening, embedded secrets and a scored report. Nothing is executed and no toolchain is bundled; radare2, jadx and apktool are used only where you already have them.
skill.name: Hanshuang Pojia — engagement executor
skill.description: Red-team and blue-team engagement executor: CTF challenges, ranges, AWD rounds, license and activation reversing, malware triage and incident response. Carries the workbench kit 2.0 protocol: lab mode, deployment verification, and the seep / IDA MCP toolchain. Execution-first — every reply opens with the artifact.
skill.apkseep.name: APK reverse engineering
skill.apkseep.description: Full-chain Android reversing: APK/AAB/DEX/SO triage, client-auth weakness review (CWE-602), minimal binary patches, Frida/RPC instrumentation, unpacking, Java2C/VMP diffing and resigned repackaging. Four hard quality gates (G1–G4) plus anti-tamper and anti-hook countermeasures.
skill.licenseBypass.name: Client licence validation bypass
skill.licenseBypass.description: Audit how a desktop client decides it is licensed: key checks, activation servers, offline token validation and the patch points that remove them, written up so the finding can be reproduced on the next build.
skill.softseep.name: Software reversing playbook
skill.softseep.description: Windows and cross-platform application reversing: entry-point discovery, string and import triage, anti-debug and virtualisation handling, then a reproducible patch or a written analysis conclusion.
skill.apkReverse.name: APK reverse (safe workflow)
skill.apkReverse.description: Guarded APK reversing workflow: decode, read the manifest and smali, reach the target method, and record every step so the change can be reviewed. Read-only by default; patching is an explicit second stage.
skill.idaReverse.name: IDA Pro reversing
skill.idaReverse.description: IDA Pro driven analysis: database setup, type and signature recovery, cross-reference walking, decompiler reads and headless batch runs. Names the IDA-side steps the plugin cannot script itself.
skill.jsPlaybook.name: JavaScript reverse playbook
skill.jsPlaybook.description: JavaScript runtime reversing: locating the signing and encryption routines, hooking them through a Frida gadget or DevTools, and turning an obfuscated bundle into a readable call chain.
skill.radare2.name: radare2 workflow
skill.radare2.description: radare2 as the default analyser: project setup, function and xref navigation, hashing and diffing, scripted batch analysis, and the r2 command sequence behind each report section.
skill.reverseEngineering.name: Reverse engineering fundamentals
skill.reverseEngineering.description: Platform-neutral reversing fundamentals: file formats, calling conventions, control-flow recovery, dynamic debugging, and how to write a conclusion that states what was proven and what was only inferred.

risk.advice.A: Nothing beyond informational rules matched. Keep the routine checks — signature, permissions, embedded endpoints — before shipping.
risk.advice.B: A few low-impact issues. Fix them in the next build; none of them changes what the app can reach on the device.
risk.advice.C: Review before trusting this build. At least one medium rule touches data access or exported surface.
risk.advice.D: Treat as untrusted until reviewed. Dangerous permissions or exported components combine into real device-level exposure.
risk.advice.E: Treat as hostile. Multiple critical rules matched; do not install or run it on a device you care about.
risk.note: Score is a weighted rule sum, not a probability.

cases.contract.title: How a case works
cases.contract.declaration: init_task writes a one-shot scope: authorisation, in-scope assets, network profile and deliverables. It is written once, so a changed scope is a new case.
cases.contract.gate: ready_for_act is derived, never passed in: authorisation granted, at least one in-scope asset, and an explicit offline sample whenever the profile is offline.
cases.contract.precedent: Every case is searchable precedent. Evidence entries are numbered E-###, decisions live under .agents/notes, and search_cases ranks both against a query.

signature.v1.detail: JAR signing over META-INF. Compatible with every Android version, weakest against tampering.
signature.v2.detail: Whole-file digest in the APK signing block. Required by Android 7 and later.
signature.v3.detail: Key rotation support, Android 9 and later.
signature.noScheme: The manifest does not name a scheme digest.
signature.limit.title: What the panel does not do
signature.limit.body: The panel reports structure only: it does not parse the certificate, resolve the signer identity or verify the digests. A present scheme means the block exists, not that the signer is trustworthy.
signature.limit.how: Ask the conversation to run apksigner verify (or codesign -dv for an IPA) and explain the signer it reports.

guide.lab.title: Lab mode
guide.lab.lead: Lab is a work-style switch shared with the chat agent. On, the agent answers in engagement shape — it opens with a runnable artefact, then verification and rollback. Off, ordinary Q&A passes through untouched.
guide.lab.off.1: Reply as a normal Q&A explanation, no delivery scaffolding.
guide.lab.off.2: No claim labels, no authorised-testing framing.
guide.lab.off.3: Best for "what is this / how does it work".
guide.lab.on.1: Five-part delivery: Locate → patch table → runnable artefact → verification → rollback.
guide.lab.on.2: Every claim marked Observed / Inferred / Assumed; unrun steps labelled NOT RUN.
guide.lab.on.3: Authorised once per target, then not re-asked.
guide.lab.case: `lab：` then e.g. recover a signing check, dump the runtime-loaded dex and review the real logic, or compare a sample family into a three-column baseline.
guide.limit.title: Limits
guide.limit.execute: The sample is never executed, unpacked to disk or uploaded.
guide.limit.network: No network access at all — the panel works offline.
guide.limit.size: One file per analysis, up to 32 MiB (the host's cap).
guide.limit.scope: Files must live inside the open project folder.
guide.limit.tools: No bundled jadx / apktool / radare2, and no shell inside the panel.
